declaration.preface:
At Transpek Industry Limited, we understand the significance of fostering a workplace rooted in fairness, respect, and dignity for all employees. As a leading player in the chemical industry, our operations span multiple sectors including pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and polymers, and we are committed to adhering to the highest standards of Labour and human rights.

Our responsibility extends beyond just meeting legal and regulatory obligations. We aim to create an inclusive work environment, promote the well-being of our employees, and ensure that labour rights are respected throughout our supply chain. This policy provides a framework that guides our practices and decisions, aligning with international labour standards and human rights principles.
declaration.declaration:
At Transpek Industry Limited, we commit to:

Upholding Labour Standards: We ensure that our employees are provided with fair wages, safe working conditions, and opportunities for professional growth.

Respecting Human Rights: We reject child and forced Labour in any form and ensure ethical treatment across all our business operations, promoting the welfare of workers and communities.

Ensuring Inclusivity: We value diversity and are committed to fostering an environment where employees are treated equally regardless of race, gender, age, religion, or any other characteristic.
declaration.scope: This Labour & Human Rights Policy applies to all employees and management of Transpek Industry Limited. Our policy is relevant across all geographic locations and is applicable to every department involved in the manufacturing and distribution of our chemical products.

Employee Health & Safety: Establish a culture of safety awareness with regular safety meetings and discussions across all levels of the organization.
Introduce mental health awareness initiatives to support employees facing psychological challenges.
Develop an employee health monitoring system to track workplace incidents and identify trends, enabling the company to take proactive measures to prevent accidents and health issues.
Working Conditions: Ensure transparent communication channels for discussing work conditions, focusing on timely responses to employee concerns.
Promote flexible work arrangements to support work-life balance.
Labour Relations: Foster labour relations by ensuring regular dialogue between management and employees on working conditions and rights.
Provide training programs on labour rights and relations, ensuring employees are informed and empowered.
Implemented a structured grievance redressal mechanism to ensure that any workplace disputes or concerns are addressed promptly and fairly.
Career Management: Develop and implement individualized career progression plans for employees, focusing on enhancing their skills and aligning their growth with the company's strategic objectives in the chemical manufacturing sector.

Introduce comprehensive training modules, workshops, and certifications tailored to industry-specific needs, such as chemical safety management, innovation in chemical processes, and operational excellence.
Establish a transparent system for internal job postings and promotions, ensuring fair access to career advancement opportunities across all levels of the organization.
Child & Forced Labour: Conduct regular supplier audits and provide training to prevent child and forced Labour throughout our supply chain.
Collaborate with industry groups and NGOs to strengthen efforts in identifying and eliminating child and forced labour practices in high-risk areas.
Diversity, Equity & Inclusion (DEI): Implement DEI programs that promote a diverse and inclusive culture where all employees feel valued and respected.
Increase representation of women in leadership roles through targeted mentorship and development programs.
Establish DEI performance metrics to regularly assess progress on diversity goals, ensuring that leadership accountability is in place.
External Stakeholder Human Rights: Respect for Local Communities: Engage with local communities to understand their concerns, ensuring that our operations respect local customs, land, and property rights.

Supplier Code of Conduct Compliance: Conduct regular audits and ensure that all suppliers and partners comply with Transpek’s Supplier Code of Conduct, emphasizing human rights protection throughout the supply chain.

Grievance Mechanisms for External Stakeholders: Develop and maintain accessible grievance mechanisms for external stakeholders, ensuring they can report human rights concerns confidentially and securely.

policy.monitoring:
Ensure the timely submission of compliance reports to regulatory authorities, outlining adherence to environmental regulations and detailing any incidents that may have occurred.

Keep thorough records of environmental audits, inspections, and assessments to demonstrate compliance with all applicable laws and regulations.

Provide clear and transparent updates to stakeholders—including employees, customers, and local communities—on environmental initiatives and progress.

Use a variety of communication channels, such as newsletters, social media, and the company website, to share achievements and address any environmental concerns raised by stakeholders.

Create dedicated internal channels for employees to report environmental concerns, incidents, or suggestions for improvement.

Foster a culture of accountability by ensuring that all reports are reviewed promptly and addressed effectively.

Develop training programs to enhance employees' understanding of environmental regulations and compliance obligations.

Promote awareness of environmental issues and best practices through workshops, seminars, and informational materials.

Implement regular risk assessments to identify potential environmental impacts and compliance risks associated with business operations.

Develop and maintain a risk management plan that outlines strategies for mitigating identified risks and ensuring compliance with environmental regulations.

Establish and promote sustainability initiatives aimed at reducing the organization's environmental footprint.

Monitor and report on the progress of sustainability goals, including energy conservation, waste reduction, and resource management.

To ensure effective governance of the Labour and Human Rights Policy, a dedicated Labour Rights Oversight Committee (LROC) will be established. The LROC will oversee compliance with labour laws, monitor workplace practices, and address any human rights concerns. Regular meetings will be held to evaluate progress, review incident reports, and recommend improvements.

The committee will comprise representatives from key departments, including human resources, legal, and operations, and will report directly to senior management to ensure alignment with organizational objectives.

Additionally, a comprehensive documentation and reporting framework will be maintained to track compliance activities, employee feedback, and stakeholder communications. This governance structure will ensure accountability and promote a proactive approach to labour and human rights management within the organization.
policy.reviewMechanism: The Managing Director will conduct an annual review of the Labour & Human Rights Policy, focusing on key performance indicators, employee feedback, and supplier audits. This process will involve data analysis, stakeholder consultation, and identification of challenges. The findings will be compiled into a report, with actionable recommendations presented to the Board of Directors. An action plan will be developed for implementation, with follow-ups scheduled to monitor progress throughout the year.
